statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Three and a half hours of live Globex trading since the Sunday restart show Nasdaq-100 futures in an orderly band of roughly 30,167.75-30,233.25, about 0.28% above Friday's 30,141.75 settle, which keeps tail in the low band, while stress stays high on the unresolved Strait of Hormuz stalemate, Brent near $88.50 and a long end that steepened into Friday's close.
recommendation: Tail sits at 12, below the block threshold, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. The Sunday restart has been observed and passed without dislocation, so the flagged observation window is the Monday U.S. cash open at 13:30-14:30 UTC, where the week's first opening auction concentrates liquidity and catalyst risk. headline: Nasdaq-100 futures hold an orderly 0.22% band since the Sunday restart; tail steady in the low band while stress stays high on Hormuz and a steeper long end
body:
Nasdaq-100 futures have now traded for three and a half hours since the weekend halt ended, and the observed path remains orderly. The September contract trades near 30,227, up about 85 points or 0.28% on Friday's 30,141.75 settle, inside a restart band of roughly 30,167.75 to 30,233.25. That band is about 0.22% wide. S&P 500 futures corroborate at about +0.09% and Dow futures are marginally higher. Delayed cross-asset context shows the same picture: index futures modestly bid, VIX futures a fraction higher, crude a touch softer and Treasury futures marginally firm. The restart therefore produced no gap discontinuity, no one-way extension and no failed-retracement sequence, which is the specific structure that would justify a higher tail reading.

The stress backdrop is unchanged and remains the reason stress sits high while tail sits low. Brent trades at $88.47, essentially flat, with the Strait of Hormuz stalemate unresolved and shipping traffic still below normal. Friday's U.S. data was soft on the consumer side, with July retail sales falling 0.6%, the largest drop in more than a year, and preliminary August UMich consumer sentiment at 51.0 against 54.5 expected. Despite that, the S&P 500 finished Friday at a record close and completed a third straight weekly gain. Rates were the mirror image: the 10-year closed near 4.696% after rising about 5.5 basis points, against a 2-year near 4.15%, so the long end did the steepening.

Under the index surface, Friday's leadership was dispersed rather than uniform. Broadcom fell about 6% as the AI trade cooled, while AMD rose 6.5% and Micron 2.3%; megacap breadth was two up and six down. Dispersion of that kind is characteristic of rotation, not of the aligned single-direction pressure that overwhelms mean reversion. VIX closed Friday at 14.25, down 2.6%, which keeps implied volatility subdued.

The week ahead is data-light before Wednesday. Empire State manufacturing prints at 12:30 UTC today with consensus near 12, followed by NAHB housing at 14:00 UTC and Net Long-term TIC Flows at 20:00 UTC. FOMC minutes from the July 28-29 meeting arrive on Wednesday at 18:00 UTC, Walmart reports Thursday and flash PMIs land Friday. None of those are today's structural risk. The flagged window is the 13:30-14:30 UTC cash open, where the week's first opening auction sets the day's reference range.

Confidence is set at 76. Current NQ level and session range, VIX, Brent, Treasury yields, the verified calendar and the shared cross-asset context are all in hand; the shared Finviz context is at the edge of its freshness window and was used only as supporting confirmation, not as live price-path evidence.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours span the tail of the CME weekend halt and the Sunday Globex restart. Published Claude assessments held EA_ON throughout. Tail rose gradually from 12 to a 17 peak around 16:00 UTC on Sunday as the reopening premium built, then eased to 15, 13 and finally 12 once the restart was observed to be orderly. Stress ran high across the whole window, peaking at 82 in the Sunday afternoon hours on the combination of Friday's weak consumer data and the Hormuz stalemate, before easing into the high sixties as the reopen passed without dislocation. Confidence improved steadily from 71 to 76 as live price-path evidence replaced pre-reopen inference, and dominant mode moved from mixed to normal at 23:00 UTC. All 24 lookback hours carry a published assessment.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours run from the Asian cash session through Europe into Monday's U.S. session and the following Globex reopen. Conditional tail stays inside the low band throughout, holding at 12 across the quiet Asian hours and peaking at 18 in the 13:00-15:00 UTC cash-open window, where the week's first opening auction concentrates liquidity and catalyst risk. Stress stays high across the horizon, easing to 66 in the quiet overnight hours and rising to 75 around the U.S. open, because the Hormuz backdrop and the soft consumer data are unresolved rather than because any one-way path has been observed. Confidence decays from 76 to 60 with distance from the current evidence. Dominant mode is normal overnight, mixed through the European and U.S. sessions, and normal again after the U.S. close. Every hour maps to EA_ON under the fixed threshold mapping.
